flashcard_questions.q: What is a customer need in business?
flashcard_questions.a: A problem that a customer could solve by buying a product or service.

flashcard_questions.q: What does value for money mean to a customer?
flashcard_questions.a: The quality of the product is fair relative to the price paid.

flashcard_questions.q: What does quality mean as a customer need?
flashcard_questions.a: How good or reliable a product is and how well it meets expectations.

flashcard_questions.q: What standard must products meet under UK law?
flashcard_questions.a: Satisfactory quality — the standard a reasonable person would regard as acceptable.
The ease with which a customer can buy and receive something, saving time and effort.

flashcard_questions.q: Which customer need does a wide range of sizes, colours and styles satisfy?
Which business delivers restaurant food from restaurants with no delivery service of their own?
What risk does a business take if it sets its price too low?
flashcard_questions.a: It may not cover its costs.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens if a business sets its price too high?
flashcard_questions.a: Customers will buy from competitors instead.

flashcard_questions.q: How does JD Sports meet the price need of its student customers?
flashcard_questions.a: Student discount periods and sale rails.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a local barber meet the convenience need of working adults?
flashcard_questions.a: Walk-ins plus online booking with evening and Saturday hours.

flashcard_questions.q: How many types of yoghurt might a typical supermarket stock?
What is the advantage of offering customers limited choice?
flashcard_questions.a: They choose more quickly, so fewer abandon the purchase.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do loyal customers help a business survive a downturn?
flashcard_questions.a: They keep buying even when times are difficult.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the ultimate risk of failing to identify customer needs?

notes: 15 cards: 5 term→definition (customer need, value for money, quality, satisfactory quality, convenience), 1 need-classification card (choice), 3 concept→named example (Deliveroo, JD Sports, local barber), 2 pricing cause→effect facts, 4 single-fact advantage/disadvantage cards. The four customer needs were not made into one list card — that would be an enumeration answer.
